notes_context:
Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0010] Check repo conventions before implementing a money-moving function: The first attempt implemented refund correctly per the issue but missed team conventions (audit entries, idempotency_key, approval threshold, float amounts) that hidden tests enforced.
  Before writing any function that moves money or changes a balance, grep the repo for sibling functions (e.g. payments.authorize) and any convention docs; mirror their audit.record calls, keyword-only params, and error codes. The issue text alone is not the full spec.
- [rb-0001] Use the project's money rounding helper for any monetary result: The first attempt returned an unrounded Decimal division and was rejected; wrapping the result in ledgerly.money.round_money fixed it.
  Before writing any function that produces a money value, check the repo's money module for a canonical rounding helper (e.g. round_money) and apply it to the final result. Python's round() and bare Decimal.quantize() use banker's rounding and violate the team convention.
- [rb-0002] Read the money module and existing sibling functions before implementing: The agent only discovered round_money, ZERO, and to_money after the review; inspecting money.py and invoice_total/line_total upfront would have avoided the rejection.
  When adding a function to a module, first read the module's imports and neighboring functions to learn the established patterns (rounding, zero constants, type coercion). Mirror those patterns in the new code.
- [rb-0003] Handle the empty/zero-denominator case explicitly: Returning ZERO when total_quantity is 0 satisfies the spec's 'invoice without lines has an average of zero' requirement and avoids division by zero.
  For weighted-average or ratio computations, guard the denominator before dividing and return the domain's zero constant (e.g. ZERO) rather than raising or returning a float 0.
- [rb-0004] Reuse existing money helpers for validation and rounding: When adding monetary input handling, delegate to the module's existing to_money/round_money/ZERO helpers instead of reimplementing conversion.
  Call to_money(unit_price) to normalize input (which also rejects bad types like floats with the project's error code), compare against ZERO for negativity, and store round_money(price). This keeps rounding and error semantics consistent with the rest of the codebase.
- [rb-0005] Guard bool before int for integer validation: In Python, bool is a subclass of int, so isinstance(True, int) is True; explicitly exclude bools when validating positive integers.
  Validate with `isinstance(quantity, bool) or not isinstance(quantity, int) or quantity <= 0` to reject True/False and non-integers like 1.5. This matches hidden-test expectations for strict integer quantity checks.

review_comments: [team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept an optional keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` (callers without a key keep working). Check the key first, before validating state: if an audit entry with the same key already exists (ledgerly.audit.events()), return the original result (for functions that return a record, the same record) without applying the operation again. Include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write. Introduced after the double-refund incident INC-204.
[team convention] Write the amount in audit entries as float(amount): the ledger service's JSON importer rejects Decimal values.

item.title: Check idempotency key before state validation
item.description: When adding idempotency to a money-moving operation, look up the audit log for the key first and return the original result before any state checks.
item.content: Scan ledgerly.audit.events() for an entry whose idempotency_key matches; if found, return the original record (or result) immediately without re-validating state or re-applying the operation. This ordering matters because a retried call may arrive after the payment has already moved to the new state, so validating state first would wrongly raise invalid_state.

item.title: Add keyword-only idempotency_key to every balance-changing function
item.description: Team convention requires an optional keyword-only idempotency_key=None on all operations that move money or change payment/credit/invoice balances.
item.content: Signature pattern: def capture(payment, at, *, idempotency_key=None) -> Payment. Callers without a key keep working unchanged. Include idempotency_key in the audit.record() call so future retries can find it.

item.title: Cast Decimal amounts to float in audit entries
item.description: The ledger service's JSON importer rejects Decimal values, so audit entries must write amounts as float(amount).
item.content: When calling audit.record(...) with a monetary amount, pass float(payment.amount) rather than the raw Decimal. This is a repo-wide convention enforced by the downstream JSON importer.
